content.title: Yankees, Max Fried blank Giants on MLB Opening Night: Live updates, reaction
content.text: Follow live reaction of the Opening Day matchup as the Yankees beat the GiantsJazz Chisholm Jr. celebrates a single during the Yankees’ Opening Night win in San Francisco Getty ImagesYankees vs. Giants — ReactionThe New York Yankees have beaten the san Francisco Giants 7-0 at Oracle Park on Opening Night of the 2026 MLB regular season. It only took the second inning for New York to post a 5-0 lead off San Francisco ace Logan Webb — including Trent Grisham’s 2-run triple. The Yankees added two more in the fifth, aided by a Giancarlo Stanton RBI single. That was more than enough for Max Fried, who tossed 6 1/3 shutout innings.Follow along for live reaction, news, analysis and highlights from today’s game.Join the conversation: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementTomorrow’s Opening Day schedule Getty ImagesAs Johnny mentioned, the real action gets going tomorrow with 11 games and 22 teams in action — here’s a full schedule (all times ET):Pittsburgh Pirates at New York Mets — 1:15 p.m. (Nationally televised on NBC)Chicago White Sox at Milwaukee Brewers — 2:10 p.m.Washington Nationals at Chicago Cubs — 2:20 p.m.Minnesota Twins at Baltimore Orioles — 3:05 p.m.Boston Red Sox at Cincinnati Reds — 4:10 p.m.Los Angeles Angels at Houston Astros — 4:10 p.m.Detroit Tigers at San Diego Padres — 4:10 p.m.Tampa Bay Rays at St. Louis Cardinals — 4:15 p.m.Texas Rangers at Philadelphia Phillies — 4:15 p.m.Arizona Diamondbacks at Los Angeles Dodgers — 8:30 p.m. (Nationally televised on NBC)Cleveland Guardians at Seattle Mariners — 10:10 p.m.And don’t worry, we’ll have all these games covered for you right here live on The Athletic.Netflix bumps take center stage in Opening Night broadcast The “first” Opening Day of 2026 has come to an end. From an in-game perspective, it was a fairly one-sided contest. New York outhit San Francisco, 10-3, one starter shoved and the other didn’t. However, all the talk will be of how Netflix approached its first MLB broadcast.Complaints about the tiny scorebug, the ad overlays causing jerseys to glitch and weird in-game cuts will undoubtedly need to be ironed out immediately. However, the streamer did capture some of the pageantry that MLB has sought for its “crown jewel” events, including some really unique pre-game introductions. Reminder: Netflix will be the home for the Home Run Derby, so what may not have worked tonight will probably look better at a more zeroed in event.This won’t be the only Opening Day of 2026, as the majority of MLB teams will kick off their seasons tomorrow, with the Toronto Blue Jays, Athletics, Colorado Rockies and Miami Marlins beginning on Friday. For baseball fans, consider this a three-day holiday. Welcome to the 162-game grind.Yankees bullpen has good first showing Getty ImagesIt’s one game — and one that was already well out of hand by the time Aaron Boone took the ball from Max Fried — but … The Yankees bullpen was seen as the weakness of this team and for one game at least, New York’s relievers did their job (although again, in very low-leverage situations) ...Jake Bird: 2/3 IP, 0 H, 0 R, 1 KBrent Headrick: 1 IP, 1 H, 0 R, 1 BB, 1 KCamilo Doval: 1 IP, 0 R, 0 HPromising signs from WellsFollowing an impressive showing on the field and some viral moments off the field while playing for the Dominican Republic in the World Baseball Classic, Yankees catcher Austin Wells picked up tonight where he left off in WBC play. Wells, the No. 9 hitter, reached base a team-high three times with two hits and a walk — he also scored a run. Wells has secured the job of Yankees starting catcher due in large part to his defense and ability to handle a pitching staff. If these are legitimate signs of him becoming a better offensive player, that would go a long way to lengthening New York’s already potent lineup.Your views: Not fond of the Netflix broadcastThe game itself was fairly undramatic, as the Yankees jumped out to a huge second-inning lead and never looked back.But the Netflix broadcast got, um, not exactly the most enthusiastic review from the readers chiming in on our “Discuss” page...SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementNice night for Stanton Imagn ImagesGiancarlo Stanton had a solid two-hit night, with both hits coming via line drive singles to center — including an absolute screamer at 114.4 mph off the bat for an RBI knock in the fifth inning.Stanton may be 36 years old now and nine years removed from his 2017 National League MVP campaign with the Miami Marlins. But the active MLB home run leader (453 and counting) still provides quite a wallop in his bat.Rough start for Webb Imagn ImagesIf Logan Webb’s past several seasons are any indication, this will be nothing but a blip as the Giants ace gets himself settled. Webb looked awesome as Aaron Judge’s Team USA teammate in the World Baseball Classic — albeit against lineups in Brazil and Canada that featured several minor leaguers — but dealt with inconsistent command of his trademark sinker and sweeper tonight, as the Yankees jumped on several first-pitch fastballs and turned them around for hits. Webb also got unlucky at points, such as Ryan McMahon’s two-run single up the middle that could have easily been an inning-ending double play if Luis Arraez was positioned more up the middle.The Giants ace should be fine going forward, even if he’ll have to deal with an inflated ERA for a bit, as it’s up to an ugly 10.80 following his five innings of work tonight.Grisham ready to build on last year Imagn ImagesAs for Trent Grisham, here’s his reaction to being asked whether the Yankees’ plan was to go after Logan Webb early …💬 “Uh, not necessarily. Just be ready for a pitch. We know he’s a strike thrower. So yeah, we executed our plan pretty well. Just be ready. “It’s a new year. I learned some things last year, showed myself a little bit of my potential and I’m just looking to build on it.”How did ABS do?There was only one ball-strike challenge issued tonight. And in the first special helmet-tap in MLB history, Yankees shortstop José Caballero challenged a call on a pitch he thought was up and in, only to discover upon the challenge that it touched the upper inside corner.Full details from Brendan Kuty blow.(Almost) All rise Imagn ImagesEvery member of the Yankees got a hit tonight — except the team captain, face of the franchise and reigning American League MVP.Yes, New York’s 10 hits tonight were scattered across eight members of the lineup — with the only exception being, of all people, Aaron Judge.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementFried grateful for offensive spaceAdorned in Netflix MVP jackets and being served hot dogs by Jameis Winston, Max Fried and Trent Grisham managed to also answer some questions — which wasn’t how it felt things would go at the start.First from Fried on a hiccup start that blossomed into domination … 💬 “I definitely was a little out of it but, you know, all the credit goes to the offense. You put on five runs, it allows me to just take a deep breath and be able to just go out there and attack.“I’m definitely more frustrated (than looking calm). I mean, it wasn’t easy. It was a grind. Like I said, they took all the pressure off of me — they were able to come out swinging and when you put up a five spot it just makes my job way easier.”Fried joins elite list Imagn ImagesMax Fried was superb tonight after a bumpy first inning. He’s had quite a journey as a Yankee, being thrust into the ace role following his free agency arrival in New York in 2025 when Gerrit Cole was forced to undergo Tommy John surgery. But he was right up there with the best showings by Yankee Opening Day starters tonight. Per MLB, David Cone (1996), Ron Guidry (1980) and Mel Stottlemyre (1967) are the only Yankee starters to match Freid’s feat of at least six shutout innings and two or fewer hits. That’s quite a list — both Guidry and Stottlemyre are enshrined in Yankee Stadium’s monument park, while Cone won four World Series with New York and remains a fan favorite as well as a beloved member of the team's local broadcast crew.Embarrassing footnote for JudgeAaron Judge is the first reigning MVP in MLB history to strike out four times on Opening Day, per MLB.Starting pitcher stats Imagn ImagesHere’s how tonight’s starting pitchers did for the Yankees and Giants …Max Fried: 6 1/3 IP, 2 H, 0 R, 1 BB, 4 K, WLogan Webb: 5 IP, 9 H, 7 R, 6 ER, 1 BB, 2 K, LFINAL: Yankees roll past Giants▶️ Heliot Ramos grounds out to shortstop, and this time Jose Caballero makes a nice play to get the out... and then Casey Schmitt flies out for the final out! The Yankees start the 2026 season with a dominant win! | Final - Yankees 7, Giants 0SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisement▶️ Jung Hoo Lee lines out to center for the first out. | Bot 9th Yankees 7, Giants 0 Imagn Images▶️ Former Giants closer and current Yankees setup man Camilo Doval, traded from San Francisco to New York at the midseason trade deadline last year, is on to slam the door in this one ... his night gets off to a tough start when Jose Caballero boots a Willy Adames ground ball to allow the leadoff runner aboard. | Bot 9th Yankees 7, Giants 0More context on Bonds turning down Yankees Getty Images Barry Bonds spent a half-inning in the Netflix booth and basically said that he would have been a Yankee if George Steinbrenner had just been a little more polite:“I would've been a Yankee, but Steinbrenner got on the phone and he called us, and he told me 'Barry, we are going to give you the money (to make you) the highest paid player at that time', but you have to sign the contract by 2 o'clock this afternoon, and I said 'Excuse me?', and I just hung the phone up.”Bonds then said he went to get lunch to think things over. Right then, he said, the Giants called him — “and I said, ‘I’m going home.’”Well… hey, maybe that's how it went down.But in Joel Sherman’s book, “Birth of a Dynasty,” he writes that the Yankees needed Danny Tartabull to go in the expansion draft to make a serious offer to Bonds. That didn't happen.In Jeff Pearlman’s Bonds biography, “Love Me, Hate Me,” he writes that the Yankees dropped out of the bidding after offering five years and $36 million. Bill Pennington’s book, “Chumps to Champs,” quotes GM Gene Michael as saying of Bonds “he said no thanks” to an offer that would have made Bonds the highest-paid player in baseball.Also, remember that George Steinbrenner was technically banned from baseball at the time of those negotiations (December 1992). That’s how Michael was able to carefully build the next Yankee dynasty without interference from The Boss. (Of course, it would surprise nobody if Steinbrenner bent the rules a little.)In any case, Bonds got a record six-year, $43.75 million contract from the Giants. During that time, the Yankees rose to become the best team in baseball, winning titles in 1996, 1998, 1999 and 2000. Their best chance to acquire Bonds may have been in a trade for Jim Leyritz and Bernie Williams ….a deal proposed by the assistant to the traveling secretary George Costanza, in season 7 of “Seinfeld.”▶️ Cody Bellinger tries to leg out an infield single on a slow roller to second, but Luis Arraez’s throw beats him by a step. Ben Rice then strikes out to end the inning. Nice work from Giants pitcher Caleb Kilian. | Mid 9th Yankees 7, Giants 0
